title: Public speaking
description: Explain an idea with a clear point, a concrete example and an ending.

challenges.title: A one-minute introduction
challenges.objective: Introduce yourself to a new group with one detail they can remember.
challenges.materials: A timer and three words on a note
steps: Write a name, a reason for being there and one specific detail.
Deliver the introduction once and time it.
Try again with a pause before the memorable detail.
challenges.criterion: The listener can repeat your purpose and one detail within one minute.
challenges.prompt: Where did you rush or lose your place?
challenges.experiment: Keep the script and change only the length of the pause.

challenges.title: Explain it to a beginner
challenges.objective: Turn a familiar process into a short explanation anyone can follow.
challenges.materials: A familiar item and a timer
steps: State the outcome first.
Explain three steps and demonstrate one.
Ask someone to retell the steps or retell them from memory after a break.
challenges.criterion: The three steps are in order and each starts with a clear action.
challenges.prompt: Which step would a beginner ask you to explain again?
challenges.experiment: Swap one abstract phrase for a concrete example.

challenges.title: Answer a meeting question
challenges.objective: Deliver a concise recommendation and respond to a likely follow-up.
challenges.materials: A current decision and a timer
steps: Write the decision in one sentence.
Speak for ninety seconds using your recommendation, evidence and trade-off.
Answer one plausible objection aloud without repeating your opening.
challenges.criterion: A listener can separate your recommendation, evidence and trade-off.
challenges.prompt: Which objection exposed a gap in your explanation?
challenges.experiment: Prepare one different example while keeping the same recommendation.

title: Communication
description: Practice listening, clear requests and useful feedback.

challenges.title: Reflect before replying
challenges.objective: Accurately reflect another person's main point.
challenges.materials: A willing partner or short spoken clip
steps: Listen for one minute without planning your reply.
Summarise the main point in a single sentence.
Ask a neutral question and revise your summary.
challenges.criterion: Your second summary captures one detail you missed initially.
challenges.prompt: What assumption did you make before asking the question?
challenges.experiment: Keep the topic and ask a more open follow-up.

challenges.title: Make a clear request
challenges.objective: Ask for a specific action with context and a deadline.
challenges.materials: Paper or a notes app
steps: Choose a small realistic request.
Write the action, reason and timing in separate lines.
Read it aloud and remove words that obscure the action.
challenges.criterion: The recipient can identify the action and decide how to respond.
challenges.prompt: What could someone still interpret in two ways?
challenges.experiment: Move the action to the first sentence and compare.

title: Photography
description: Use framing and light to make the subject easy to read.

challenges.title: Frame a single subject
challenges.objective: Use a deliberate background to separate one subject.
challenges.materials: A camera and an everyday object
steps: Make an initial photo at eye level.
Move around the object until the background simplifies.
Capture another frame and look at both as thumbnails.
challenges.criterion: The subject stays legible in the second thumbnail.
challenges.prompt: Which background element did you remove and what changed?
challenges.experiment: Hold exposure and framing steady while you change only the camera height.

challenges.title: Find soft window light
challenges.objective: Compare direct and reflected light on the same object.
challenges.materials: An object, a window and white paper
steps: Place the object beside indirect window light.
Photograph the shadow side.
Hold white paper opposite the window and repeat from the same spot.
challenges.criterion: Both frames show what the reflector changed on the shadow side.
challenges.prompt: Which details became easier to see?
challenges.experiment: Move the paper half as far away and compare.

title: Drawing
description: Make everyday objects recognisable through shape and proportion.

challenges.title: Build from simple shapes
challenges.objective: Draw an object by comparing its largest shapes.
challenges.materials: Paper, pencil and a mug
steps: Use a rectangle and an ellipse to block in the mug.
Compare its width to its height before adding the handle.
Draw a second version using the same viewpoint.
challenges.criterion: Your handle joins the mug at two deliberate points.
challenges.prompt: Which proportion changed between drawings?
challenges.experiment: Use the rim width as the unit for every other measurement.

challenges.title: Draw the negative space
challenges.objective: Use spaces around an object to check proportions.
challenges.materials: Paper, pencil and a chair
steps: Sketch the outer contour from one viewpoint.
Draw the spaces between the legs and under the seat.
Compare those spaces against the chair and revise two lines.
challenges.criterion: The gaps between legs have a deliberate shape and relative size.
challenges.prompt: Which space helped you correct the object most?
challenges.experiment: Check the largest gap first before drawing any details.

title: Cooking fundamentals
description: Organize ingredients and practice flavour balance with no-cook exercises.

challenges.title: Set up a cold snack station
challenges.objective: Arrange ingredients and utensils in the order you need them.
challenges.materials: A washable surface, clean utensils and ready-to-eat ingredients
steps: Wash your hands and clear the work surface.
Lay out ingredients in the order you will use them.
Assemble a small snack and note each time you had to stop for a missing item.
challenges.criterion: The next attempt can run without looking for an ingredient.
challenges.prompt: Which interruption could you remove with a better layout?
challenges.experiment: Move the most frequently used ingredient closest to you.

challenges.title: Compare two simple dressings
challenges.objective: Taste how varying one ingredient changes balance.
challenges.materials: Food-safe bowls, spoons, oil and lemon juice if suitable for you
steps: Start with equal amounts of oil in two bowls.
Add a small measured amount of lemon to the first and a little more to the second.
Taste separately with clean spoons and write which you prefer.
challenges.criterion: Your notes describe the difference without using only ‘better’.
challenges.prompt: What did more acid change about the flavour?
challenges.experiment: Use the preferred version as a baseline and change one ingredient.

title: Creative writing
description: Use concrete details and revision to make a scene vivid.

challenges.title: Write a place in three senses
challenges.objective: Let specific details establish a place without naming it.
challenges.materials: Paper or a notes app
steps: Choose a real or imagined place.
Write three short observations from three senses.
Remove the place name and replace a general adjective with a detail.
challenges.criterion: A reader can infer something about the setting from the details.
challenges.prompt: Which detail was easiest to imagine?
challenges.experiment: Keep the scene and replace one sight detail with a sound.

challenges.title: Cut a scene to its turning point
challenges.objective: Revise a short scene around the moment something changes.
challenges.materials: A draft of around 150 words
steps: Underline the moment a character decides or discovers something.
Remove one sentence that delays that moment.
Read both versions aloud and pick the one with a clearer change.
challenges.criterion: The revision makes the change identifiable without adding explanation.
challenges.prompt: What did the cut change about the pacing?
challenges.experiment: Move one sensory detail to just before the turning point.

title: Digital literacy
description: Build confidence organizing files and validating small spreadsheets.

challenges.title: Build a practice filing system
challenges.objective: Create a folder and naming convention you can use again.
challenges.materials: A file manager and three harmless sample files
steps: Make a folder called Practice and two subfolders by purpose.
Rename each sample using a consistent date and topic pattern.
Try to retrieve one from search and one from its containing folder.
challenges.criterion: All three samples are easy to distinguish without opening them.
challenges.prompt: Which filename would still make sense six months from now?
challenges.experiment: Use one shorter naming pattern and repeat the retrieval task.

challenges.title: Verify a spreadsheet total
challenges.objective: Create a simple table and check the result independently.
challenges.materials: A spreadsheet app and five fictional amounts
steps: Enter five amounts next to five labels.
Use SUM for the total and verify it mentally or with a calculator.
Change one amount and check how the result changes.
challenges.criterion: The total updates by the exact change made to the input.
challenges.prompt: What mistake would your independent check catch?
challenges.experiment: Insert a sixth row and check whether the formula includes it.

title: Personal organisation
description: Turn a crowded list into actions that fit the time you have.

challenges.title: Choose tomorrow’s first action
challenges.objective: Prepare an action you can start in five minutes.
challenges.materials: Paper or your task list
steps: Write three things competing for your attention.
Select the one with the greatest consequence if delayed.
Describe the first visible action and decide when to do it.
challenges.criterion: You can start without making another decision.
challenges.prompt: What might prevent you from getting started?
challenges.experiment: Place one required item where you will see it.

challenges.title: Compare estimates with reality
challenges.objective: Improve a planning estimate by observing the actual time.
challenges.materials: A timer and two simple chores
steps: Estimate each chore separately.
Time the chores and write down any interruptions.
Update your estimate and add a buffer for the uncertain part.
challenges.criterion: Your revised estimate explains a specific difference.
challenges.prompt: Did the task or the interruption take longer than expected?
challenges.experiment: Measure setup time separately during the next attempt.

title: Basic home DIY
description: Build safe measurement and planning habits with craft materials.

challenges.title: Measure before cutting
challenges.objective: Check a mock-up before buying or fitting anything.
challenges.materials: Cardboard, ruler, pencil and blunt craft scissors
steps: Measure a small object twice from the same reference edge.
Mark the measurements on cardboard.
Cut the cardboard with blunt scissors and check the fit.
challenges.criterion: The cardboard model matches the intended size within your marked tolerance.
challenges.prompt: Which measurement was hardest to repeat?
challenges.experiment: Mark the reference edge before you measure.

challenges.title: Make a removable layout plan
challenges.objective: Compare arrangements before moving anything heavy.
challenges.materials: Paper, a ruler and pencil
steps: Sketch a tabletop as a rectangle.
Cut paper shapes to represent three lightweight objects.
Try two layouts and identify the one that leaves the clearest work area.
challenges.criterion: Your plan improves access to at least one regularly used item.
challenges.prompt: Which item made the layout difficult?
challenges.experiment: Try a different position for that item and compare remaining space.

title: Everyday problem-solving
description: Test one explanation at a time and compare observable outcomes.

challenges.title: Test one change
challenges.objective: Define a small recurring nuisance and test one possible cause.
challenges.materials: A notebook and a low-risk everyday problem
steps: Describe when the issue happens and what you observe.
List two possible causes and choose one to test.
Change one thing and compare the result to the usual pattern.
challenges.criterion: Your record distinguishes what you observed from what you inferred.
challenges.prompt: What else might explain the result?
challenges.experiment: Repeat the same test before changing another variable.

challenges.title: Compare two options fairly
challenges.objective: Use consistent criteria to choose between two practical options.
challenges.materials: Paper and an everyday choice
steps: List two feasible options.
Select three criteria before scoring either option.
Score both options and identify which criterion could change your decision.
challenges.criterion: Each score has a short reason and the same scale is used for both options.
challenges.prompt: Which score depends on the weakest evidence?
challenges.experiment: Gather one fact that could change the weakest score.
